item.title: Year 3 at work and tech
item.description:
Year 3 at work and tech

Work and tech stuff since last blog post has continued to be around multiple different projects with multiple project titles. Now, it’s 3 years since I started working at a company, so it was time to collect and write down everything I’ve been working on in the past year to see where I’m at. This blog is kind of a draft, still.

Table of contents

  • Internal tools at work
    • Software Assessment report app (Maximus)
    • Cloud infrastructure for Service Reporting
    • Dashboard for product vulnerabilities
    • Loadstats
    • Local server infrastructure at work
  • B2B stuff at work
  • Side projects and other
    • tweetlists.app
    • Bootstrat
    • RAGs
  • Future

Internal tools at work

  1. Software Assessment report app

My first project at work—an app named Maximus—for a “bug dashboard report generator” entered its third year of service in production. At the time of writing my previous work blog post, it had already become a full-stack web app that parallelly ingested data across endpoints to a serial optimization and filtering pipeline, so work lately was mostly around how to make the filtering pipeline faster. There was a part that sequentially loaded each bug’s webpage on the internal bug tracking platform on selenium which I rewrote using asyncio + httpx and made it parallel, bringing down a part that took around 20 minutes to 3 minutes on average.

item.title: Notes from my first workplace as an employee
item.description:
Hey, we’re back.

The cadence of these notes will vary like a meandering river as it was not easy to connect different things and also keep the same voice – “I am not an expert; I’m just writing it down as I fare forward and figure it out” throughout the blog. I also feel this blog post lacks a certain standard of emotional density that I thought this would have when I envisioned writing it. Nevertheless, the deliverables of an average blog post on this site: candid accounts of experiences and reflections, with an edge for optimism, can be easily observed even by the accidental audience on this blog post.
